 Medium
 Large
 Print The storm was located about 600km east of Chennai on Tuesday evening. CHENNAI: Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ over the central parts of the south Bay of Bengal and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal, moved slowly northwards at a speed of 3kmph during the past six hours. It lay centred over the same region at 11.30am on November 17, 2026, near latitude 12.3°N and longitude 85.7°E. The storm was located about 600km east of Chennai, 640km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 650km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 660km south-southeast of Join conversation
 View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments
 Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines 
 Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 780km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal by the evening of November 17. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19. Continuing its northwestward movement, the storm is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 120–130kmph and gusts reaching 145kmph.
